iOS 27 is expected to be full of new features for Siri and Apple Intelligence. There are, however, a few other changes in store for some of the most-used iPhone apps. Here are a few new details from a Bloomberg report published today.

New iOS 27 tidbits

While much of the Bloomberg report recaps what we already know about iOS 27, there are a few interesting new tidbits worth calling out.

  • The Find My app is getting a “subtle visual refresh” that includes new icons in the navigation tab bar.
  • The “Clean Up” feature in the Photos app is getting “significant improvements during the iOS 27 cycle.”
  • Apple is testing “natural language prompt-based editing of photos so you can ask via voice or text for specific edits, like cropping or changing colors.” This feature, however, might not be available in the first version of iOS 27.
  • iOS 27 includes a new animation for incoming notifications. “They now slide in from the left side of the screen, aligning with the new gesture system: Users swipe down from the left to open the Notification Center because swiping down from the center now opens the Search or Ask AI panel.”

Apple will officially announce the update on Monday, kicking off WWDC with a special keynote at 10 a.m. PT/1 p.m. ET. I’ll be inside Apple Park for the festivities and will have full coverage right here on 9to5Mac.

What iOS 27 new features are you most excited to see? Is there anything on your wishlist that hasn’t been rumored yet? Let us know down in the comments.
